findings.change: Slack POST and signature metadata are rejected before schema and SDK initialization; read/HMAC admission is capped at 256 KiB and 3 seconds; only signed events may resolve bot identity; private admitted-request cache avoids double consumption and rechecks freshness. One fixed-capacity byte buffer and one read-plus-HMAC deadline race bound retained allocation and promise reactions independently of empty/one-byte chunk counts.
findings.verification: Actual Chat SDK with mock fetch verifies unsigned/invalid requests cause zero provider calls, valid URL challenge and Slash work, tampered/invalid UTF-8 and oversized/stalled/aborted bodies reject; actual full Worker without D1 binding proves rejection before schema. A fragmented signed UTF-8 stream at its exact byte cap preserves HMAC; an endless empty-chunk stream terminates at its monotonic deadline without awaiting cancellation.

findings.change: A shared HTTP(S)-only presentation boundary strips URL username/password/query/fragment in public links, Slash, rich cards and repeated error/reason text. Probe URL and history remain unchanged. Both stored primary/fallback URLs are replaced in full before generic URL matching, escaping, clipping or truncation, longest URL first to cover overlapping prefixes and raw query spaces/quotes.
findings.verification: Real SQLite renderer and actual notification regressions verify synthetic credential-bearing probe URLs in stored error, reason and components do not leak through status, incident, RSS, Slash, rich Slack or Discord payloads; valid detail routing parameters remain. Regression reprints both primary/fallback URLs with raw query spaces and quotes in error/reason/component/name/description; no synthetic secret marker survives any tested renderer or notification payload.

findings.change: A common fail-closed hidden monitor predicate covers public dashboard, RSS, incident and shared Slash status; hidden incident IDs return 404 before DB lookup. Availability role filtering is preserved. Public cache keys are partitioned by presentation version, Worker version and hidden monitor configuration.
findings.verification: Real SQLite renderer tests verify hidden monitor names and history stay out of each shared view and direct enumeration; history and monitor state remain unchanged; cache tests demonstrate old responses cannot bypass privacy or rendering changes.

native_worker.test: actual Worker rejects unsigned Slack traffic before its D1 schema gate and without provider I/O

limitations: Local verification only; parent will coordinate repository-wide review and any separately authorized release.
Public monitor privacy now also applies to shared authenticated Slash status; privileged monitoring administration remains in the authenticated management API.
production_deployment: Not deployed; local verification and commit only.
